summary: A Russian refinery in Syzran, Samara Oblast, has caught fire following drone attacks. Ukraine is receiving significant military aid, including a German-funded order for 50,000 Shrike FPV drones. Ukrainian leadership is undergoing political restructuring as President Zelenskyy announces plans to replace the Prime Minister and law enforcement leadership.
key_points: A refinery in Syzran, Samara Oblast, belonging to PJSC Rosneft, caught fire following drone attacks (Source: @UkraineNow/82587).
Germany is financing the purchase of 50,000 Shrike FPV drones for Ukraine, featuring US-made Auterion software for autonomous target engagement (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31567).
President Zelenskyy announced plans to replace Prime Minister Sviridenko and implement personnel changes in the government and law enforcement agencies (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31566).
Ukrainian drone forces struck 10 tankers and 4 ferries, contributing to a total of 90 Russian vessels targeted over the last week (Source: @UkraineNow/82591).
A drone strike on an industrial enterprise in Kryvyi Rih resulted in two fatalities (Source: @UkraineNow/82588).
In Kherson, a drone dropped an explosive device in the Korabel district, killing one person and injuring two (Source: @UkraineNow/82588).
A drone strike on a food industry enterprise in Dnipro was reported with no preliminary casualties (Source: @UkraineNow/82588).
In Sumy, a strike resulted in six deaths and 42 injuries (Source: @UkraineNow/82588).

sections.executive_summary: A Russian refinery in Syzran, Samara Oblast, has caught fire following drone attacks. Ukraine is receiving significant military aid, including a German-funded order for 50,000 Shrike FPV drones. Ukrainian leadership is undergoing political restructuring as President Zelenskyy announces plans to replace the Prime Minister and law enforcement leadership.

points: President Zelenskyy announced the replacement of Prime Minister Sviridenko and upcoming personnel changes within the government and law enforcement agencies (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31566).
Germany is financing the purchase of 50,000 Shrike FPV drones, equipped with Auterion software to autonomously track and engage moving targets (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31567).
Ukraine is expected to receive Patriot missile systems under a contract with Germany no earlier than 2028 (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31564).
Poland has transferred 5 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, with a provision for 50 more in case of threat (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31564).
Ukrainian drone forces struck 10 tankers and 4 ferries, part of a larger campaign that hit 90 Russian vessels in the last week (Source: @UkraineNow/82591).
A refinery in Syzran, Samara Oblast, part of PJSC Rosneft, caught fire following drone attacks (Source: @UkraineNow/82587).
Russian forces attacked public transport in Kherson, hitting a minibus and a stop, resulting in two civilian injuries (Source: @UkraineNow/82593).
Authorities in the Chernigov region are reportedly preparing operations to detain at least 70 pro-Russian residents in border areas (Source: @tass_agency/384930).
A bus traveling from Stakhanov to Moscow in the LNR was attacked by the AFU, reportedly injuring two women (Source: @tass_agency/384936).
Enemy forces have advanced near Zhalizne (Source: @DeepStateUA/23636).
Russian tactical aviation launched guided aerial bombs toward the Kharkiv region from the east (Source: @kpszsu/68222).
UAVs were reported flying near Velyshane in the Kharkiv region on a south-southeast course (Source: @kpszsu/68252).
UAVs were observed near Shevchenkove heading toward Pechenihy/Chuhuiv (Source: @kpszsu/68223).
In Crimea, Dzhankoy and the Dzhankoy district have been without electricity for seven days (Source: @UkraineNow/82592).
Water supply in Dzhankoy is restricted to specific hours due to fuel shortages and high costs (Source: @UkraineNow/82592).
The Azov Sea port in Rostov Oblast was struck by an FP-1 drone several days ago (Source: @eRadarrua/100724).
A Su-34 launched a missile maneuver (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68904).
A Su-57 launched a missile maneuver (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68902).
A Shahed drone entered the Podilskyi district of Poltava from the north (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68893).
A Kh-31P missile was reported heading toward Odesa/Chornomorsk (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68891).
36 enemy UAVs heading to Moscow were destroyed since the start of the day (Source: @tass_agency/384914).

key_developments: A Rosneft refinery in Syzran, Samara Oblast, caught fire following drone strikes (Source: @UkraineNow/82587).
Germany is financing 50,000 Shrike FPV drones for Ukraine, featuring autonomous target engagement software (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31567).
President Zelenskyy announced plans to replace Prime Minister Sviridenko and reform law enforcement (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31566).
Ukrainian drones struck 10 tankers and 4 ferries, part of a week-long campaign hitting 90 vessels (Source: @UkraineNow/82591).
A drone strike in Kryvyi Rih killed two people at an industrial enterprise (Source: @UkraineNow/82588).
A drone strike in Sumy resulted in six deaths and 42 injuries (Source: @UkraineNow/82588).
Dzhankoy and surrounding areas in Crimea remain without electricity for a seventh day (Source: @UkraineNow/82592).
sections.threat_assessment: The operational environment is characterized by high-intensity drone warfare targeting both industrial infrastructure and civilian areas. The strike on the Syzran refinery indicates continued long-range capability against Russian energy assets. The influx of 50,000 autonomous FPV drones from Germany will likely increase the lethality of Ukrainian tactical operations.
sections.regional_response: Ukraine is undergoing significant political restructuring as President Zelenskyy moves to replace the Prime Minister and law enforcement leadership. International support remains high, evidenced by German financing for large-scale drone procurement and Polish transfers of Patriot missiles.
sections.intelligence_notes: The use of autonomous software in Shrike FPV drones represents a significant technological shift in UAV engagement. The targeting of civilian transport and infrastructure in Kherson and Sumy highlights the ongoing impact of kinetic strikes on non-combatant populations.
